name: python-module-anchoring-is-defensive
body: `parse_args` composes each `--module` value as `args.root.join(value)`, so `run`'s canonical-root anchoring is defensive rather than the CWD fix the bug write-up described — for a relative scan root the value arrives already root-joined, and the old and new orderings resolve to the same real path for every traced input (plain relative, `..`-bearing under a relative or absolute root, a symlinked root, and a symlinked root with a `..`); the only real delta is on canonicalize failure, where the fallback switches from a raw possibly-relative value to the anchored absolute (emission-invisible, since a nonexistent dir admits nothing); upgrade by moving the join out of `parse_args` when the resolution rule must be provable from `run` alone.
